result:
I would sever the connection between the human ego and being right.

Right now, the human brain processes a challenge to a deeply held belief almost the same way it processes a physical threat. That single piece of wiring is behind an astonishing amount of the world’s misery. It is why bad ideas survive long after they are disproven, why wars drag on just to avoid losing face, why people rationalize cruelty once they’ve committed to a side, and why conversations between people who disagree usually turn into trench warfare.

If discovering you were wrong didn’t feel like a humiliation or a threat to your identity—if it instead felt like the quiet relief of setting down something heavy—almost everything else would start to fix itself. 

Humanity doesn't really suffer from a shortage of intelligence, resources, or even compassion. There is already more than enough of all three to build a remarkable world. What breaks things, over and over, is the instinct to protect the story you’ve already told yourself, even when it’s hurting everyone—including you.
